title: Area of Triangles
contentObjective: I can find the area of a triangle using the formula A = ½ × base × height.
languageObjective: I can explain my steps using the words base, height, area, and perpendicular.

noticeAndWonder.context: This is the firm's blueprint for a park. A rectangular plot is split by a diagonal path into two triangular garden beds that will be filled with soil.
wonderStarters: I wonder what would happen if…

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Painting a Cabin
revealWordProblem.text: The front of this A-frame cabin is a triangle with a base of 34 ft and a height of 23¾ ft. Find the area of the triangular front that needs to be painted.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Area = ½ × base × height = ½ × 34 × 23¾. First, 23¾ = 23.75, so 34 × 23.75 = 807.5. Then take half: 807.5 ÷ 2 = 403.75. The triangular front of the cabin has an area of 403.75 square feet.

turnAndTalk.question: The triangular garden bed has a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet. Which measurement is the height, and how is it different from the slanted side?
turnAndTalk.kernel: The height is the perpendicular distance from the base to the top corner.

stems.en: The height is the ___ distance from the base to the top corner.
stems.es: La altura es la distancia ___ desde la base hasta la esquina de arriba.

stems.en: It is different from the slanted side because ___.
stems.es: Es diferente del lado inclinado porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students identify the height as the perpendicular (straight-up, 90-degree) distance from the base to the opposite vertex, not the slanted side.
turnAndTalk.extend: Does it matter which side of the garden triangle you call the base? Justify your thinking using the formula A = 1/2 x b x h.
extendStems: It ___ matter which side is the base because ___.
No matter which base I choose, the area is the same since ___.

turnAndTalk.question: On the grid your triangle (base 12, height 8) fits inside a 12 by 8 rectangle. Why do we divide by 2 to find the triangle's area?
turnAndTalk.kernel: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

stems.en: A triangle is half of a ___ with the same base and height.
stems.es: Un triángulo es la mitad de un ___ con la misma base y altura.

stems.en: So the area is 1/2 times 12 times 8, which equals ___.
stems.es: Entonces el área es 1/2 por 12 por 8, que es ___.

stems.en: The rectangle's area is ___, so the triangle is ___.
stems.es: El área del rectángulo es ___, entonces el triángulo es ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: A strong answer states the triangle is half of the 12 x 8 = 96 rectangle, so the triangle area is 48 sq ft, and connects the 1/2 to that halving.
turnAndTalk.extend: Two different triangles both have area 48 sq ft. Must they have the same base and height? Justify or give a counterexample.
extendStems: They ___ have the same base and height because ___.
A counterexample is a triangle with base ___ and height ___, which also gives ___.

turnAndTalk.question: The homeowner paints a triangular A-frame wall with base 20 ft and height 14 ft; one can covers 50 sq ft. Talk through how many cans are needed.
turnAndTalk.kernel: Find the triangle area first, then divide by what one can covers.

stems.en: The wall's area is 1/2 times 20 times 14, which equals ___ square feet.
stems.es: El área de la pared es 1/2 por 20 por 14, que es ___ pies cuadrados.

stems.en: She needs ___ cans because ___ divided by 50 equals ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Students compute area = 140 sq ft, then 140 / 50 = 2.8, and reason she must round up to 3 cans to cover the whole wall.
turnAndTalk.extend: Why can't the homeowner buy exactly 2.8 cans? Explain what rounding up means in this real situation and how it changes the leftover paint.
extendStems: She must round up to ___ cans because ___.
The leftover paint covers about ___ sq ft, since ___.

turnAndTalk.question: During practice on Area of Triangles, what strategy did you use when a problem felt tricky?
turnAndTalk.kernel: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

stems.en: A triangle is half of a ___ with the same base and height.
stems.es: Un triángulo es la mitad de un ___ con la misma base y altura.

stems.en: I knew my answer was reasonable because ___.
stems.es: Supe que mi respuesta era razonable porque ___.

turnAndTalk.listenFor: Listen for students naming a specific strategy tied to 6.GR.1 — not just "I multiplied." They should connect steps to the key idea.
turnAndTalk.extend: How would you help a classmate who made the common mistake from today's lesson? Use one vocabulary word.
extendStems: I would tell them to ___ first because ___.
The mistake happens when you ___ instead of ___.

vocabulary.definition: The space inside a triangle. Formula: A = 1/2bh, using the perpendicular height.
vocabulary.definitionEs: El espacio dentro de un triángulo. Fórmula: A = 1/2bh, usando la altura perpendicular.
vocabulary.visual: A = 1/2bh; if b = 8 and h = 5, A = 20 square units.

vocabulary.definition: A side of the triangle you use to find the area.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un lado del triángulo que usas para hallar el área.
vocabulary.visual: If the bottom of a triangle is 10 cm, then b = 10 cm in the formula A = ½ × b × h
vocabulary.cloze: The side of a triangle used as the bottom for measuring area is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: The straight-up distance from the base to the top corner.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La distancia recta desde la base hasta la esquina de arriba.
vocabulary.visual: A dashed vertical line from the top point straight down to the base at a 90° angle — like dropping a plumb line
vocabulary.cloze: The perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex is the ___.

vocabulary.definition: How much space is inside a flat shape.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cuánto espacio hay dentro de una figura plana.
vocabulary.visual: A triangle with b = 8 and h = 6 has area = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 sq units — exactly half the rectangle around it
vocabulary.cloze: The amount of flat space inside a triangle is its ___.

vocabulary.definition: Two lines that meet to make a square corner (90 degrees).
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos líneas que se unen formando una esquina recta (90 grados).
vocabulary.visual: The corner of a book or a door frame — the edges meet at exactly 90°, shown by a small square symbol
vocabulary.cloze: Two lines that meet at a 90° angle are ___.

examples.text: Two lines meeting at a 90° angle
examples.why: Perpendicular lines form a right angle.
Those are parallel lines, not perpendicular.

vocabulary.definition: A shape made by putting two or more simple shapes together.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una figura formada al juntar dos o más figuras simples.
vocabulary.visual: A house shape = a rectangle (the walls) + a triangle (the roof); total area = rectangle area + triangle area
vocabulary.cloze: A shape made of two or more basic shapes combined is a ___.

vocabulary.definitionEs: Una regla matemática escrita con símbolos.
vocabulary.visual: A = ½ × b × h means Area equals one-half times base times height; for b = 12 and h = 8, A = 48
vocabulary.cloze: A math rule written with symbols, like A = ½ × b × h, is a ___.

visual.title: The Park Plot on the Blueprint
visual.caption: The diagonal path (from corner A to corner C) splits this 12 ft by 8 ft plot into two garden beds. What do you notice about the two beds it makes?

launch.narrative: Your architecture firm is designing a park with triangular garden beds. The client wants to know exactly how much soil to order, which means calculating the area of each triangular section. The first garden has a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet.
launch.contextImage: Architectural blueprint with triangular garden sections marked in green
noticePrompts: What shape are the garden beds?
What measurements do we need to find the area?
How is the area of a triangle related to the area of a rectangle?
wonderPrompts: Why do we divide by 2 when finding the area of a triangle?
Does it matter which side we call the base?

conceptIntro.heading: How do we find the area of a triangle?
conceptIntro.intro: A triangle has three sides. The base is one side, and the height is the straight-up (perpendicular) distance from the base to the top corner.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height. A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My triangular garden has a base of 12 feet and a height of 8 feet.
I write the formula: A = ½ × base × height.
I put in the numbers: A = ½ × 12 × 8.
I take half: ½ × 96 = 48. So the area is 48 square feet.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now a smaller triangle: base = 10 cm, height = 6 cm.
Now take half: what is ½ × 60? Yes, 30.
So the area is 30 square centimeters.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: Next you will plot the triangle on a grid and see how it fits inside a rectangle.
Remember: multiply base × height, then take half.

explore.instructions: Plot the vertices of a triangle with base 12 and height 8 to visualize the garden. Place points at (0, 0), (12, 0), and (6, 8).
explore.label: Plot the three vertices of the triangular garden bed.

discourse.prompt: The triangle fits inside a 12 × 8 rectangle. How does the triangle's area compare to the rectangle's area?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The area of the triangle is ___ the rectangle because A = 1/2 × ___ × ___ = ___ square feet.

optional.stem: A triangular window in the firm's lobby has a base of 10 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
optional.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 sq ft. The triangle is half of the 10 × 6 = 60 rectangle it fits inside.
choiceFeedback: One pair of parallel sides = trapezoid.
Does this have one or two pairs?
Check which sides actually match up parallel.
optional.stemEs: Una ventana triangular en el vestíbulo de la firma tiene una base de 10 ft y una altura de 6 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
optional.explanationEs: A = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 10 × 6 = ½ × 60 = 30 sq ft. El triángulo es la mitad del rectángulo de 10 × 6 = 60 en el que cabe.
hints: A triangle covers exactly half of the rectangle that has the same base and the same height.
Use A = ½ × base × height: multiply the two measurements first, then take half of that product.
Start with 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft for the whole rectangle, then take half of 60 to finish.
hintsEs: Un triángulo cubre exactamente la mitad del rectángulo que tiene la misma base y la misma altura.
Usa A = ½ × base × altura: multiplica primero las dos medidas y luego toma la mitad de ese producto.
Empieza con 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft para el rectángulo completo y después toma la mitad de 60 para terminar.

optional.stem: A triangular roof panel on the blueprint has a base of 7 ft and a height of 4 ft. What is its area?
optional.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 7 × 4 = ½ × 28 = 14 sq ft. Multiply base × height first (28), then take half (14).
choiceFeedback: A trapezoid has TWO parallel bases.
Add both bases in the formula.
The height is perpendicular between the bases.
optional.stemEs: Un panel triangular del techo en el plano tiene una base de 7 ft y una altura de 4 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
optional.explanationEs: A = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 7 × 4 = ½ × 28 = 14 sq ft. Multiplica primero base × altura (28) y después toma la mitad (14).
hints: The area of a triangle is A = ½ × base × height, and the ½ is there because a triangle is half of a rectangle.
Multiply the base by the height first, then cut that result in half.
Multiply 7 × 4 to find the surrounding rectangle's area, then take half of that product for the triangle.
hintsEs: El área de un triángulo es A = ½ × base × altura, y el ½ está ahí porque un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo.
Multiplica primero la base por la altura y después divide ese resultado a la mitad.
Multiplica 7 × 4 para hallar el área del rectángulo que lo rodea y luego toma la mitad de ese producto para el triángulo.

optional.label: Match each triangular plan on the blueprint to its area. Use A = ½ × base × height.
optional.hint: Use the formula A = ½ × base × height.
optional.explanation: Every card on the blueprint is a triangle, so each area is ½ × base × height: ½ × 10 × 6 = 30, ½ × 7 × 4 = 14, ½ × 9 × 8 = 36, ½ × 16 × 3 = 24, ½ × 5 × 8 = 20, and ½ × 11 × 2 = 11 sq ft.
optional.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta del plano es un triángulo, así que cada área es ½ × base × altura: ½ × 10 × 6 = 30, ½ × 7 × 4 = 14, ½ × 9 × 8 = 36, ½ × 16 × 3 = 24, ½ × 5 × 8 = 20 y ½ × 11 × 2 = 11 sq ft.
optional.labelEs: Une cada diseño triangular del plano con su área. Usa A = ½ × base × altura.

optional.instructions: An intern at the firm gave two answers for each triangular wall. Sort each answer into the CORRECT area (½ × base × height) or the FORGOT THE HALF mistake (just base × height).
optional.explanation: Each wall appears twice — once with the ½ applied and once without. 18 × 6 = 108, so the correct area is 54 sq ft; 20 × 5 = 100, so the correct area is 50 sq ft; 14 × 8 = 112, so the correct area is 56 sq ft. In every pair, the 'forgot the half' answer is exactly double the correct one.
optional.explanationEs: Cada muro aparece dos veces: una con el ½ aplicado y otra sin él. 18 × 6 = 108, así que el área correcta es 54 sq ft; 20 × 5 = 100, así que el área correcta es 50 sq ft; 14 × 8 = 112, así que el área correcta es 56 sq ft. En cada par, la respuesta que 'olvidó la mitad' es exactamente el doble de la correcta.
hints: A triangle covers half of the rectangle around it, so the correct area of each wall is half of base × height.
For each wall, multiply base × height first. That product is the 'forgot the half' answer; half of it is the correct one.
Start with the wall of base 18 and height 6: multiply 18 × 6, then halve it. Compare both numbers to that wall's two cards.
hintsEs: Un triángulo cubre la mitad del rectángulo que lo rodea, así que el área correcta de cada muro es la mitad de base × altura.
Para cada muro, multiplica primero base × altura. Ese producto es la respuesta que 'olvidó la mitad'; la mitad de ese producto es la correcta.
Empieza con el muro de base 18 y altura 6: multiplica 18 × 6 y luego toma la mitad. Compara los dos números con las dos tarjetas de ese muro.
optional.instructionsEs: Un pasante de la empresa dio dos respuestas para cada muro triangular. Clasifica cada respuesta en el área CORRECTA (½ × base × altura) o en el error de SE LE OLVIDÓ LA MITAD (solo base × altura).

optional.stem: On the blueprint, a triangular garden bed has a base of 11 ft and a height of 6 ft. What is its area?
optional.explanation: A = ½ × base × height = ½ × 11 × 6 = ½ × 66 = 33 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: That's base × height — a triangle is half of that.
You added base and height — use ½ × base × height instead.
Recompute ½ × 11 × 6 carefully.
optional.stemEs: En el plano, un jardín triangular tiene una base de 11 ft y una altura de 6 ft. ¿Cuál es su área?
optional.explanationEs: A = ½ × base × altura = ½ × 11 × 6 = ½ × 66 = 33 sq ft.
hints: Every triangle's area comes from A = ½ × base × height.
With an odd base, it is easier to multiply base × height first and take half at the end.
Start with 11 × 6 for the rectangle that surrounds the triangle, then take half of that result.
hintsEs: El área de todo triángulo se obtiene con A = ½ × base × altura.
Con una base impar, es más fácil multiplicar primero base × altura y tomar la mitad al final.
Empieza con 11 × 6 para el rectángulo que rodea al triángulo y después toma la mitad de ese resultado.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — Find the Half-Area Mistake
optional.correctWork: The intern stopped at base × height = 16 × 9 = 144, but that is the area of the whole rectangle. A triangle is only half of that rectangle, so you must still take half: ½ × 144 = 72 sq ft.
hints: A triangle fits inside a matching rectangle. Is 144 the rectangle or the triangle?
The formula has a ½ in it. The intern multiplied 16 × 9 but never took half — finish by computing ½ × 144.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2: encuentra el error de la mitad del área
optional.explanation: Multiplying 16 × 9 = 144 is only half the job — that product is the area of the rectangle that surrounds the triangle. The formula still has a ½ waiting to be used, so the triangular wall is ½ × 144 = 72 sq ft.
optional.explanationEs: Multiplicar 16 × 9 = 144 es solo la mitad del trabajo: ese producto es el área del rectángulo que rodea al triángulo. La fórmula todavía tiene un ½ esperando, así que el muro triangular mide ½ × 144 = 72 sq ft.

approaching.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 10 cm and height 6 cm?
approaching.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 square centimeters.
choiceFeedback: Add 5 + 9, divide result by 2, then × 4.
The bases are the parallel sides.
Follow A = (b₁ + b₂) ÷ 2 × h exactly.
hints: You have a base of 10 cm and a height of 6 cm — a triangle needs only those two, plus one special step.
A triangle is half of a rectangle: use A = ½ × b × h. If you only multiply, your answer is twice too big.
Multiply 10 × 6, then take half of the product. Area units are square centimeters.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo con base de 10 cm y altura de 6 cm?
approaching.explanationEs: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 10 × 6 = 30 centímetros cuadrados.
hintsEs: Tienes una base de 10 cm y una altura de 6 cm: un triángulo solo necesita esas dos, más un paso especial.
Un triángulo es la mitad de un rectángulo: usa A = ½ × b × h. Si solo multiplicas, tu respuesta sale al doble.
Multiplica 10 × 6 y luego saca la mitad del producto. Las unidades de área son centímetros cuadrados.

approaching.stem: A triangle has an area of 24 sq ft and a base of 8 ft. What is the height?
choiceFeedback: Add the bases: 6 + 8 = 14.
Divide by 2, then multiply by 5.
Do not forget any step.
hints: The area (24 sq ft) and base (8 ft) are given — you're solving backwards for the height.
Simplify first: ½ × 8 = 4, so the equation becomes 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 by 4 to find the height in feet.
approaching.stemEs: Un triángulo tiene un área de 24 sq ft y una base de 8 ft. ¿Cuál es la altura?
hintsEs: Te dan el área (24 pies²) y la base (8 pies): estás despejando la altura al revés.
Simplifica primero: ½ × 8 = 4, así que la ecuación se vuelve 24 = 4 × h.
Divide 24 entre 4 para hallar la altura en pies.

approaching.stem: Why do we divide by 2 when finding the area of a triangle?
choices: A triangle is exactly half of a rectangle with the same base and height
The base is always twice the height
We always divide area formulas by 2
approaching.explanation: A triangle with base b and height h fits inside a rectangle with the same base and height. The triangle covers exactly half the rectangle, so A = ½ × b × h.
choiceFeedback: Which two sides are parallel?
The height is perpendicular to them.
Identify bases and height correctly.
hints: Think about drawing a diagonal across a rectangle — what two shapes does it create?
Compare a triangle to a rectangle with the same base and height. How much of the rectangle does the triangle cover?
Sketch a rectangle, draw one diagonal, and shade one triangle. What fraction of the rectangle did you shade?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Por qué dividimos entre 2 al hallar el área de un triángulo?
approaching.explanationEs: Un triángulo con base b y altura h cabe dentro de un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura. El triángulo cubre exactamente la mitad del rectángulo, así que A = ½ × b × h.
choicesEs: Un triángulo es exactamente la mitad de un rectángulo con la misma base y la misma altura
La base siempre es el doble de la altura
Siempre dividimos entre 2 las fórmulas de área
hintsEs: Piensa en trazar una diagonal en un rectángulo: ¿qué dos figuras se forman?
Compara un triángulo con un rectángulo de la misma base y altura. ¿Qué parte del rectángulo cubre el triángulo?
Dibuja un rectángulo, traza una diagonal y sombrea un triángulo. ¿Qué fracción del rectángulo sombreaste?

approaching.stem: What is the area of a triangle with base 14 ft and height 6 ft?
choiceFeedback: Exactly ONE pair of parallel sides is a trapezoid.
TWO pairs would be a parallelogram.
Count the parallel pairs.
hints: Base 14 ft and height 6 ft — remember what makes a triangle's area different from a rectangle's.
Use A = ½ × b × h: compute the full product first, then halve it. Area needs square units.
Find 14 × 6, then take half of that product. Write the units as sq ft.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuál es el área de un triángulo con base de 14 ft y altura de 6 ft?
hintsEs: Base de 14 pies y altura de 6 pies: recuerda qué hace distinta el área de un triángulo de la de un rectángulo.
Usa A = ½ × b × h: calcula primero el producto completo y luego sácale la mitad. El área necesita unidades cuadradas.
Halla 14 × 6 y luego saca la mitad de ese producto. Escribe las unidades como pies².

approaching.instructions: Use the formula A = ½ × b × h to find the area of each triangle.
approaching.hint: For each row, multiply base × height, then take half: A = ½ × b × h.
hints: Each sail row gives one base and one height — the blank Area column is yours to fill.
These are triangles, so use A = ½ × b × h: multiply, then take half. There are no bases to add here.
Sail A: multiply 6 × 8, then halve it. Do the same steps for Sail B with 10 and 5.
approaching.explanation: Both sails are triangles, so each area comes from A = ½ × b × h. Sail A: 6 × 8 = 48, and half of 48 is 24 sq ft. Sail B: 10 × 5 = 50, and half of 50 is 25 sq ft. There are no bases to add here — a triangle has just one base and one height.
approaching.explanationEs: Las dos velas son triángulos, así que cada área sale de A = ½ × b × h. Sail A: 6 × 8 = 48, y la mitad de 48 es 24 sq ft. Sail B: 10 × 5 = 50, y la mitad de 50 es 25 sq ft. Aquí no hay bases que sumar: un triángulo tiene solo una base y una altura.
approaching.instructionsEs: Usa la fórmula A = ½ × b × h para encontrar el área de cada triángulo.
hintsEs: Cada fila de velas da una base y una altura; la columna vacía de Área es tuya para llenar.
Estos son triángulos, así que usa A = ½ × b × h: multiplica y luego saca la mitad. Aquí no hay bases que sumar.
Vela A: multiplica 6 × 8 y luego saca la mitad. Haz los mismos pasos para la Vela B con 10 y 5.

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake
approaching.correctWork: The student multiplied 9 × 4 = 36, but that is the area of the whole rectangle around the triangle. A triangle is only half of that rectangle, so the answer must still be cut in half: ½ × 36 = 18 sq ft.
hints: Look at the formula: A = ½ × base × height. Does the final answer include the ½?
9 × 4 = 36 is the rectangle's area, not the triangle's. What is ½ × 36?
approaching.explanation: Multiplying 9 × 4 = 36 is a good first move, but the answer stops there. 36 sq ft is the area of the rectangle that surrounds the triangle, and a triangle covers only half of that rectangle. Taking the ½ once gives A = ½ × 36 = 18 sq ft.
approaching.explanationEs: Multiplicar 9 × 4 = 36 es un buen primer paso, pero la respuesta se queda ahí. 36 sq ft es el área del rectángulo que rodea al triángulo, y un triángulo cubre solo la mitad de ese rectángulo. Al tomar la mitad una vez se obtiene A = ½ × 36 = 18 sq ft.

onLevel.hint: Use A = ½ × b × h; work backwards for missing values.
hints: Gardens A and D are missing area; Gardens B and C are missing a base or height — those need backwards steps.
Missing area: ½ × b × h. Missing base or height: double the area first, then divide by the measurement you know.
Garden B: double 27 to get 54, then divide 54 by the base 9 to find the height.
onLevel.explanation: Two rows run forward and two run backward. Garden A: ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft, and Garden D: ½ × 15 × 4 = 30 sq ft. When the base or height is missing, double the area first: Garden B, 27 × 2 = 54, then 54 ÷ 9 = 6 ft of height; Garden C, 35 × 2 = 70, then 70 ÷ 10 = 7 ft of base.
onLevel.explanationEs: Dos filas van hacia adelante y dos van hacia atrás. Garden A: ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft, y Garden D: ½ × 15 × 4 = 30 sq ft. Cuando falta la base o la altura, primero duplica el área: Garden B, 27 × 2 = 54, y luego 54 ÷ 9 = 6 ft de altura; Garden C, 35 × 2 = 70, y luego 70 ÷ 10 = 7 ft de base.
hintsEs: A los Jardines A y D les falta el área; a los Jardines B y C les falta una base o una altura, y esos necesitan pasos al revés.
Falta el área: ½ × b × h. Falta la base o la altura: duplica primero el área y luego divide entre la medida que conoces.
Jardín B: duplica 27 para obtener 54 y luego divide 54 entre la base 9 para hallar la altura.

onLevel.label: Match each shape to its area. Watch the rule: triangles use A = ½ × base × height, but parallelograms and rectangles use A = base × height (do NOT take half).
onLevel.hint: Calculate each area using the trapezoid formula, then compare.
hints: The label warns you: triangles take half, but parallelograms and rectangles do not.
For each card, first name the shape, then pick the rule: triangle ½ × b × h; the others just b × h.
Start with 'Triangle b=8, h=6': take half of 8 × 6. Then 'Parallelogram b=5, h=4' is just 5 × 4.
onLevel.explanation: Read the shape name before choosing a rule. The triangles take half: ½ × 8 × 6 = 24, ½ × 10 × 8 = 40, and ½ × 12 × 5 = 30 sq units. The parallelograms and the rectangle do not: 5 × 4 = 20, 9 × 2 = 18, and 7 × 3 = 21 sq units.
onLevel.explanationEs: Lee el nombre de la figura antes de elegir la regla. Los triángulos toman la mitad: ½ × 8 × 6 = 24, ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 y ½ × 12 × 5 = 30 sq units. Los paralelogramos y el rectángulo no: 5 × 4 = 20, 9 × 2 = 18 y 7 × 3 = 21 sq units.
onLevel.labelEs: Une cada figura con su área. Cuidado con la regla: los triángulos usan A = ½ × base × altura, pero los paralelogramos y los rectángulos usan A = base × altura (NO tomes la mitad).
hintsEs: La etiqueta te avisa: los triángulos llevan mitad, pero los paralelogramos y los rectángulos no.
Para cada tarjeta, primero nombra la figura y luego elige la regla: triángulo ½ × b × h; los demás solo b × h.
Empieza con 'Triángulo b=8, h=6': saca la mitad de 8 × 6. Luego 'Paralelogramo b=5, h=4' es solo 5 × 4.

onLevel.instructions: Calculate the area of each triangle. Sort by whether the area is greater than 30 sq units or not.
onLevel.hint: Find which measurement is height (perpendicular), then calculate.
hints: Each card shows its area after the arrow — your task is comparing that number to 30.
'Greater than 30' means strictly more than 30. A card that equals exactly 30 goes in the '30 or less' group.
First card: b=10, h=8 gives A=40. Decide if 40 is more than 30, place it, then check each card the same way.
onLevel.explanation: Each card already shows its area, so the sort is just a comparison to 30. The areas 40, 35, and 36 are greater than 30. The areas 27 and 28 are smaller, and the b=10, h=6 card lands on exactly 30 — which is not GREATER than 30, so it belongs in the 'Area ≤ 30 sq units' group.
onLevel.explanationEs: Cada tarjeta ya muestra su área, así que la clasificación es solo una comparación con 30. Las áreas 40, 35 y 36 son mayores que 30. Las áreas 27 y 28 son menores, y la tarjeta de b=10, h=6 cae exactamente en 30, que no es MAYOR que 30, así que va en el grupo 'Area ≤ 30 sq units'.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Calcula el área de cada triángulo. Clasifícalos según si el área es mayor que 30 unidades cuadradas o no.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta muestra su área después de la flecha: tu tarea es comparar ese número con 30.
'Mayor que 30' significa estrictamente más de 30. Una tarjeta que dé exactamente 30 va en el grupo de '30 o menos'.
Primera tarjeta: b=10, h=8 da A=40. Decide si 40 es más que 30, colócala y revisa cada tarjeta igual.

onLevel.instructions: A triangle has a base of 10 ft and an area of 35 sq ft. Place a point at the height. (Hint: 35 = ½ × 10 × h → 35 = 5h → h = 7)
onLevel.label: Find the missing height: b = 10, A = 35
onLevel.hint: Rearrange the formula to solve for base or height.
hints: You're placing the height. With a base of 10, half of the base is 5 — that number simplifies everything.
Rewrite A = ½ × b × h as 35 = 5 × h, using ½ × 10 = 5.
Divide 35 by 5 and place your point at that height.
onLevel.explanation: Start from A = ½ × b × h and substitute what you know: 35 = ½ × 10 × h. Since ½ × 10 = 5, the equation simplifies to 35 = 5h, so h = 35 ÷ 5 = 7. The point belongs at 7 ft on the line.
onLevel.explanationEs: Empieza con A = ½ × b × h y sustituye lo que ya sabes: 35 = ½ × 10 × h. Como ½ × 10 = 5, la ecuación se simplifica a 35 = 5h, así que h = 35 ÷ 5 = 7. El punto va en 7 ft de la recta.

onLevel.title: Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: There is only ONE ½ in the formula, not two. The student halved both the base and the height. Multiply base × height first, then take half just once: 12 × 7 = 84, then ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.
hints: How many times does the ½ appear in A = ½ × base × height — once or twice?
Multiply 12 × 7 = 84 first, then take half a single time: ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft.
onLevel.explanation: There is only ONE ½ in A = ½ × base × height, but the calculation halved the base and the height separately. Multiply first, then halve a single time: 12 × 7 = 84, and ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft. Halving twice cuts the area to a quarter of the rectangle, which is why 21 came out as exactly half of the true answer.
onLevel.explanationEs: En A = ½ × base × altura hay solo UN ½, pero el cálculo tomó la mitad de la base y la mitad de la altura por separado. Multiplica primero y toma la mitad una sola vez: 12 × 7 = 84, y ½ × 84 = 42 sq ft. Tomar la mitad dos veces reduce el área a la cuarta parte del rectángulo, y por eso 21 resultó ser exactamente la mitad de la respuesta correcta.

extending.title: Find the Area Error
extending.correctWork: 14 × 9 = 126, then ½ × 126 = 63 sq m. The student added 14 + 9 = 23 instead of multiplying 14 × 9 = 126.
hints: Look at Step 4. What operation should happen between 14 and 9?
14 × 9 ≠ 23. The student added instead of multiplied.
extending.explanation: The setup A = ½ × 14 × 9 is written correctly, but the calculation added 14 + 9 = 23 instead of multiplying. Base and height must be multiplied: 14 × 9 = 126, and then ½ × 126 = 63 sq m.
extending.explanationEs: El planteamiento A = ½ × 14 × 9 está bien escrito, pero el cálculo sumó 14 + 9 = 23 en vez de multiplicar. La base y la altura se multiplican: 14 × 9 = 126, y luego ½ × 126 = 63 sq m.

extending.prompt: A rectangle is 12 ft by 8 ft. A diagonal line cuts it into two triangles. What is the area of each triangle? Explain how the triangle area formula relates to the rectangle area formula.
extending.sentenceFrame: The rectangle's area is ___ because ___. Each triangle's area is ___ because a diagonal splits a rectangle into ___ equal triangles, so A = ½ × ___ × ___ = ___.
extending.hint: Write the formula with given numbers; solve step by step.
hints: Start with the rectangle: its area comes from 12 × 8. The diagonal splits that area into two identical pieces.
Each triangle keeps the same base (12) and height (8) as the rectangle — so its area is half the rectangle's.
Compute 12 × 8, halve it for one triangle, then check with ½ × 12 × 8. Explain why both paths give the same number.
extending.explanation: The rectangle's area is 12 × 8 = 96 sq ft, and one diagonal cuts it into two identical triangles, so each triangle is 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. The formula says the same thing: each triangle keeps the rectangle's base of 12 and height of 8, and A = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft. The ½ in the triangle formula IS that diagonal cut.
extending.explanationEs: El área del rectángulo es 12 × 8 = 96 sq ft, y una diagonal lo corta en dos triángulos idénticos, así que cada triángulo mide 96 ÷ 2 = 48 sq ft. La fórmula dice lo mismo: cada triángulo conserva la base de 12 y la altura de 8 del rectángulo, y A = ½ × 12 × 8 = 48 sq ft. El ½ de la fórmula del triángulo ES ese corte diagonal.
extending.promptEs: Un rectángulo mide 12 pies por 8 pies. Una línea diagonal lo corta en dos triángulos. ¿Cuál es el área de cada triángulo? Explica cómo se relaciona la fórmula del área del triángulo con la del rectángulo.
hintsEs: Empieza con el rectángulo: su área sale de 12 × 8. La diagonal parte esa área en dos piezas idénticas.
Cada triángulo conserva la misma base (12) y altura (8) del rectángulo, así que su área es la mitad de la del rectángulo.
Calcula 12 × 8, sácale la mitad para un triángulo y luego comprueba con ½ × 12 × 8. Explica por qué ambos caminos dan el mismo número.

extending.instructions: A triangular garden has base 16 ft and height 10 ft. The bar model shows the rectangle area (whole) and the triangle area (part). Fill in the values.
extending.label: Rectangle 16×10 = 160 sq ft split into two equal triangles of 80 sq ft each
extending.hint: A triangle covers half its surrounding rectangle: A = ½ × b × h.
hints: The whole bar is the rectangle wrapped around the triangle: base 16 ft times height 10 ft.
A triangle covers exactly half of its surrounding rectangle, so the bar splits into two equal parts.
Compute 16 × 10 for the whole bar, then split it into two equal parts — one part is the garden's area.
extending.explanation: The whole bar is the rectangle that wraps around the triangular garden: 16 × 10 = 160 sq ft. A diagonal splits that rectangle into two identical triangles, so the bar breaks into two equal parts of 80 sq ft. The garden is one of those parts, which matches ½ × 16 × 10 = 80 sq ft.
extending.explanationEs: La barra completa es el rectángulo que envuelve al jardín triangular: 16 × 10 = 160 sq ft. Una diagonal parte ese rectángulo en dos triángulos idénticos, así que la barra se divide en dos partes iguales de 80 sq ft. El jardín es una de esas partes, lo que coincide con ½ × 16 × 10 = 80 sq ft.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Triangles is forgetting the ½ — students multiply base × height like a rectangle and stop there, or they use the triangle's slanted side instead of the perpendicular height that's already given. Always check: did I take half, and did I use the straight-up height, not the slanted side?

exitTicket.stem: A triangle has a base of 11 inches and a height of 8 inches. What is its area?
choiceFeedback: That's base × height — remember the ½ for a triangle.
You added instead of multiplying — use ½ × base × height.
Right number, wrong unit — area is square inches.
hints: Base 11 inches, height 8 inches — and it's a triangle, so there's one extra step after multiplying.
Use A = ½ × b × h. Multiplying without the ½ gives the rectangle's area, which is double the triangle's.
Find 11 × 8, then take half of the product. Label it in square inches.
